labelled_by: Claude Fable 5.2 alone, blind to the models' scores; no second rater (every other Claude model is a candidate); no label was set by a person
decision: Anand, 10 Nov 2026, 22:24-22:33 IST (#175): the tone gate's second round, labelled by Fable (option B), prompt v3, models Haiku then Sonnet then Opus
how: the labeller read the 30 passages' stored text by chunk id through the read-only dev connector and scored each on its own text and section, by the tone section of GUIDE.md with prompt v3's three rules; reasons are paraphrases (no transcript text in this file)

labels.reason: A long-range vision of cross-border grid linking, with a diplomatic hurdle noted; no judgement on results, demand, margins or the near outlook.
Reassurance that the company's component supplies are not what is holding up a customer's programme; a delivery-status clarification, not a view on results or outlook.
Explains why a low-profit activity is not being pursued; a strategic stance on a business they are not in, not a judgement on their own performance.
Procedural account of why the accounts were late, then an input-cost picture described as mixed, with rises in some materials offset by easing in others.
Only a list of participants' names and titles; no management language to score.
Leadership change framed with enthusiasm and an expectation of future growth, synergies and efficiency gains; forward-looking optimism but nothing delivered yet.
Trade-duty headwind met with belief in eventual relief, but timing admitted as unknowable and the situation called early; hope and uncertainty roughly offset.
A newly returned leader's greeting and thanks; pleasantries with no judgement on results, demand, margins or outlook.
Borrowings reduced through tight cash management and further cost and cash improvement expected, qualified by temporary pressures from maintenance and ramp-up.
Admits demand shrank late in the period, utilisation suffered and a mix headwind lies ahead, softened by a plan to rebuild margins through named levers.
Commentary on a rival product category: small today, prone to price erosion, and being watched; an industry assessment, not a view on own results or outlook.
A hand-off that relays an analyst's question to a colleague; procedural, with no judgement expressed.
Brief clarification of a one-off levy that inflated a cost line plus a stated expectation of a further fall; factual, with no evaluative language.
Explains when an acquired unit entered the accounts and why comparisons differ; purely factual.
Describes how a minority-stake venture fund operates and declines to commit either way on a suggestion; descriptive and non-committal.
Order intake described as the best ever, with growth called robust and spread across home and overseas markets; confident and unqualified.
All-time-high revenue and sequential operating gains are set against lower yearly profit, cost pressure and investment losses; positives and negatives offset.
Reaffirms a moderate growth aim and voices ambition to lift market share soon, while noting recent pricing moves need time to settle; hedged optimism.
Service initiatives are said to have delivered good results and worked well for the product range; positive judgement, but confined to these offerings.
Rule change judged neutral, but management flags slower small-depositor growth, higher outflow assumptions and a system trend running against its funding aim.
Lending units summed up as having a very good quarter with sound asset quality, tempered by mention of tougher competition, attrition and a steady-not-stellar label.
A progress report on technology adoption, staffing and rollout dates; a factual update without a judgement on results, demand or margins.
Explains that a pricing-structure change depends on regulators and cannot be done alone; procedural and regulatory, no tone on performance.
Market leadership, rising shares and continued core growth are claimed, but with a fading key product and possible timing gaps before new launches fill in.
Management calls the period outstanding on every measure, with top-line growth praised without qualification despite a tight market backdrop.
A filing cover letter with addresses and links; no management commentary on performance.
Reports losses, calls the year among the hardest for the industry and concedes an operational failure that hit results badly; no offset on performance.
Mostly recited figures, but performance and profitability are judged favourably and investor appetite is highlighted; weather difficulties noted yet outweighed.
A recital of lending, income, profit and asset-quality figures with comparisons; almost no evaluative language from management.
Outlines where sales capability exists or must be built for a launch and declines to detail spending; factual, plus contact boilerplate.
